t:
(a) Patent Term Extension for the Badge of the American Legion.—The term of the design patent numbered 54,296 (for the badge of the American Legion) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, with all the rights and privileges pertaining to such patent. 
    (b) Patent Term Extension for the Badge of the American Legion Women’s Auxiliary.—The term of the design patent numbered 55,398 (for the badge of the American Legion Women’s Auxiliary) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, with all the rights and privileges pertaining to such patent. 
    (c) Patent Term Extension for the Badge of the Sons of the American Legion.—The term of the design patent numbered 92,187 (for the badge of the Sons of the American Legion) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, with all the rights and privileges pertaining to such patent.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that naming a non-federal organization (the American Legion) makes this participation. But the section only extends design patent terms directly by statute, conferring a benefit on outside groups. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue, so no outside party takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: The term of the design patent numbered 54,296 (for the badge of the American Legion) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act

opus.w: Congress itself renews and extends three design patents. No federal agency has to consult anyone, hold a hearing, take public comment or issue regulations, and no one gains a right to sue or object. The American Legion is an outside organization, but it only receives the benefit of the extension and takes no part in any federal decision, so the section does not cross the participation threshold.
opus.s: The term of the design patent numbered 54,296 (for the badge of the American Legion) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, with all the rights and privileges pertaining to such patent.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The American Legion and its affiliated groups are private, non-federal organizations named in the section, so it can look like outsiders are involved. That reading fails the definition. Congress extends the patents directly by statute, and no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue is involved. The organizations simply benefit from the extension.

qwen_chat.w: This section unilaterally extends patent terms for specific badges. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with the American Legion or any other outside party. The decision is made by Congress via statute, without any procedural requirement for outside input.
qwen_chat.s: The term of the design patent numbered 54,296 (for the badge of the American Legion) is renewed and extended for a period of 14 years beginning on the date of enactment of this Act, with all the rights and privileges pertaining to such patent.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that extending patents for the American Legion (a non-profit organization) involves some form of consultation or participation with that organization. However, the text simply states that the patent terms are renewed and extended by statute. There is no requirement for the government to consult with the American Legion, nor is there any mechanism for public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties regarding this decision. The decision is made unilaterally by Congress through the enactment of the Act.
